definitions.explanation: The direction opposite to the one currently being discussed or traveled. Commonly used for trains, roads, and general orientation.

examples.japanese: {逆方向|ぎゃくほうこう}の{電車|でんしゃ}に{乗|の}ってしまった。
examples.english: I accidentally got on a train going in the opposite direction.

examples.japanese: この{道|みち}は{逆方向|ぎゃくほうこう}だから、{引|ひ}き{返|かえ}そう。
examples.english: This road goes the wrong way, so let's turn back.

examples.japanese: {風|かぜ}が{逆方向|ぎゃくほうこう}から{吹|ふ}いてきたので、{自転車|じてんしゃ}を{漕|こ}ぐのが{大変|たいへん}だった。
examples.english: The wind was blowing from the opposite direction, so it was tough pedaling the bicycle.

notes:
USAGE:
A compound noun formed from {逆|ぎゃく} (reverse, opposite) + {方向|ほうこう} (direction). Very common in daily conversation, especially when talking about transportation mistakes or navigation.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {逆方向|ぎゃくほうこう}に{進|すす}む (to go in the opposite direction)
- {逆方向|ぎゃくほうこう}の{電車|でんしゃ} (a train going the other way)
- {逆方向|ぎゃくほうこう}に{走|はし}る (to run in the opposite direction)
- {逆方向|ぎゃくほうこう}から{来|く}る (to come from the opposite direction)
